provides: Geohash proximity search and geocoding, no GDAL/PostGIS/spatial database: a hierarchical location tree (flat lat/lon points with an auto-encoded geohash and a stable cross-service UUID), a proximity search facade (nearby/radius/bbox) behind one swappable backend, and a geocoder proxy (forward/structured/reverse) behind a provider merge-registry, throttled, cached and spend-ledgered per call, plus a coarse IP-geolocation verb behind its own provider registry, so a map opens on a real place before the browser's position prompt is answered.

curated.summary: Which proximity-search backend serves nearby/radius/bbox. Default runs geohash prefix expansion over the primary database (no extra infra); a Redis GEOSEARCH side-index backend ships for the hot set; Elasticsearch/Solr are named stubs (README.md 'Proximity search facade', conf.py).

Default geocoding provider name, resolved through the GEOCODERS merge-registry (built-in photon/nominatim, or a registered name). google/yandex are key-gated stubs a host implements with its own PAYG keys (conf.py, MODULE.md 'Geocoder provider seam').

Which locator places a visitor for GET api/v1/ip, through the IP_LOCATORS merge-registry (maxmind reads an offline .mmdb; static answers one configured point). No answer falls back to IP_FALLBACK_CENTER / MAP_DEFAULT_CENTER rather than failing.

extension_points.name: SEARCH_BACKEND
extension_points.summary: REPLACE seam: implement the GeoSearchBackend protocol (nearby/radius/bbox) and point the setting at your class (search/base.py, MODULE.md 'Search backend seam').

extension_points.name: GEOCODERS
extension_points.summary: MERGE registry ({name: dotted_path}) over BUILTIN_GEOCODERS (photon/nominatim/google/yandex); None/'' removes a builtin name. Also extendable at runtime via register_geocoder() (geocoding/providers.py, MODULE.md 'Geocoder provider seam').

extension_points.name: GEOCODE_CACHE_POLICY
extension_points.summary: REPLACE seam: GeocodeCachePolicy ABC (should_cache/lookup/store); default LedgerCachePolicy answers from the GeocodeCache ledger table within GEOCODE_CACHE_TTL_DAYS (geocoding/cache.py, MODULE.md 'Geocode cache seam').

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: SerializerSeamMixin on geocoder views (response_serializer_class) and LocationViewSet (a plain DRF ModelViewSet, serializer_class/get_serializer_class) — subclass and remount to swap (views.py, geocoding/views.py, MODULE.md 'Serializer seams').

extension_points.name: IP_LOCATORS
extension_points.summary: MERGE registry ({name: dotted_path}) over BUILTIN_IP_LOCATORS (maxmind/static); None/'' removes a name. Implement IpLocator.locate(ip) -> IpLocation | None, where None means 'I do not know' and is a normal answer (ipgeo/providers.py).

extension_points.name: IP_CLIENT_IP_RESOLVER
extension_points.summary: REPLACE seam: request -> str | None, the whole proxy-trust decision. The default counts X-Forwarded-For from the RIGHT by IP_TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH, so a forged prefix is inert (ipgeo/client_ip.py).

surface.name: build_map_config
surface.intent: Assemble the location picker's configuration from STAPEL_GEO — tile template, the attribution the ODbL licence obliges the map to display, the zoom envelope, the operating bbox, the search-as-you-type discipline. Reach for this in a server-rendered host instead of reading the MAP_* settings one by one, so the page and the geo-react picker cannot disagree about what the map is allowed to do.

surface.name: apply_formatter
surface.intent: Stamp properties.formatted on a GeocodeProperties using the configured ADDRESS_FORMATTER, swallowing a formatter's exception into a null label. A custom Geocoder implementation calls this on every feature it maps, so third-party providers carry the same display line as the built-in ones.

surface.name: format_address
surface.intent: Build the one-line human label for a geocoded place from its components, in the country's own postal order (house number before or after the street). Already applied to every feature this library returns as properties.formatted — call it directly only when you hold GeocodeProperties you assembled yourself, and override it fleet-wide via STAPEL_GEO['ADDRESS_FORMATTER'] rather than reformatting per product.
instead_of: each product joining name/street/housenumber/city/country its own way

surface.name: street_line
surface.intent: Just the street half of an address — street and house number joined in the order that country writes them ('7 Tverskaya Street' vs 'Тверская улица, 7'). Reach for this when you render address components in your own layout and only need the one line the anglocentric default gets backwards.

surface.name: register_geocoder
surface.intent: Register (or, with None/"", unregister) a geocoder provider by dotted path at runtime, from an AppConfig.ready() — the fork-free way to add a provider without going through the STAPEL_GEO['GEOCODERS'] setting. Runtime registrations win over both the setting and the built-ins.

surface.name: registered_geocoders
surface.intent: The effective name -> dotted-path geocoder registry (built-ins merged under the GEOCODERS setting merged under runtime register_geocoder() calls). Reach for this instead of re-deriving the merge yourself — e.g. to list available providers in an admin dropdown or a diagnostics endpoint.

surface.name: geocode
surface.intent: The one call path the geocoder proxy views use: provider resolution by name, cache lookup (GEOCODE_CACHE_POLICY), the provider call, and an always-written GeocodeCache spend-ledger row. Call this instead of calling a Geocoder provider directly — a direct call skips the cache and, more importantly, skips the accounting row that makes provider spend visible.
instead_of: calling a Geocoder provider's search/reverse/structured directly, bypassing the cache and the spend ledger

surface.name: get_geocoder
surface.intent: Instantiate the geocoder provider registered under a name (default STAPEL_GEO['GEOCODER']), validated as a Geocoder subclass. Reach for this instead of resolving the GEOCODERS registry and import_string-ing the class yourself when you need a raw provider call outside the cached/ledgered geocode() path.

surface.name: resolve_point
surface.intent: Turn one coordinate pair into a CONFIRMABLE place in a single round trip: the display line, the address components, the geohash to store, the runner-up candidates, and optionally the nearest known Location rows. This is the server half of 'detect my position' and of a dropped map pin. Call this instead of chaining geocode('reverse') + your own label assembly + your own geohash call — that chain is exactly what every product was rebuilding.
instead_of: geocode('reverse') followed by hand-assembled address text and a separate geohash call
a composer that just stores raw latitude/longitude and never resolves an address

surface.name: distance_km
surface.intent: True great-circle (haversine) distance between two geohashes, decoded to their cell centres and rounded to 2 decimals — correct across the antimeridian and near the poles. Call this instead of writing your own haversine formula or approximating distance from geohash prefix similarity.
instead_of: geohash prefix-similarity used as a distance proxy

surface.name: encode
surface.intent: Encode a lat/lon pair to a geohash string of the given precision (pure arithmetic, no DB, no GDAL) — the same helper Location.save() and the geo.geohash_encode comm Function call underneath. Reach for this in-process instead of round-tripping through the comm bus, and instead of pulling in a second geohash library.

surface.name: nearby
surface.intent: The proven 9-cell geohash neighbour-widening top-K search — equator/antimeridian/pole safe, with a proven-coverage stopping rule and an authoritative full-scan fallback. This is what PostgresGeoSearchBackend runs underneath; a custom SEARCH_BACKEND implementation should call this instead of re-deriving geohash neighbour widening, which is exactly where the pole/antimeridian edge cases hide.
instead_of: a hand-rolled geohash neighbour-widening / cell-expansion search

surface.name: rank_by_proximity
surface.intent: Sort any iterable of geohash-carrying candidates nearest-first against a target geohash (candidates without a geohash sort last). The building block for a custom STAPEL_GEO['SEARCH_BACKEND']: use it to rank your own candidate set instead of writing another haversine sort.

surface.name: fallback_location
surface.intent: The centre to open on when nothing is known about the caller — IP_FALLBACK_CENTER, or MAP_DEFAULT_CENTER when it is unset. Reach for it in a surface that needs the same 'no opinion' answer the IP verb gives, so the two cannot drift apart.

surface.name: get_ip_locator
surface.intent: Resolve the configured IP locator by NAME through the IP_LOCATORS merge registry and instantiate it. Reach for it when you need the provider itself (a management command seeding a cache, a test); ordinary callers want locate_ip, which adds the cache and the fallback.
instead_of: importing a locator class directly and pinning a provider

surface.name: locate_ip
surface.intent: Place a client IP coarsely, or return the deployment's fallback centre — the one call behind GET api/v1/ip. Never raises for input and never returns a location to store on a record: it exists so a map or a search opens somewhere real before the browser's position prompt is answered (or after it is refused). Reach for it server-side when a page needs a starting centre.
instead_of: hardcoding a city centre in a frontend
calling a third-party IP-geolocation API from your own view

surface.name: get_backend
surface.intent: Instantiate the configured STAPEL_GEO['SEARCH_BACKEND'], validated against the GeoSearchBackend protocol (nearby/radius/bbox). Reach for this instead of import_string-ing the setting yourself when you need the raw backend object — e.g. RedisGeoSearchBackend's own index()/rebuild() maintenance methods, which the services.py facade does not expose.

surface.name: bbox
surface.intent: Locations inside a lat/lon rectangle, antimeridian-aware (min_lon > max_lon wraps) — the in-process equivalent of the geo.bbox comm Function. Call this instead of a hand-written lat/lon BETWEEN query, which silently breaks on a box crossing ±180°.
instead_of: a hand-written lat/lon BETWEEN query with no antimeridian handling

surface.name: nearby_by_coords
surface.intent: Top-K nearest Location summaries to a coordinate pair (nearest-first), through the configured SEARCH_BACKEND — the in-process equivalent of the geo.nearby comm Function. Call this directly when you are already in the same process instead of round-tripping through comm.

surface.name: nearby_by_geohash
surface.intent: Top-K nearest Location summaries to a geohash (decoded to its cell centre) — the in-process equivalent of geo.nearby's geohash form. Prefer this over decoding the geohash yourself and calling nearby_by_coords.

surface.name: nearby_rows_by_coords
surface.intent: Same search as nearby_by_coords but returns ORM Location rows (each carrying a .distance_km attribute) instead of summary dicts — reach for this when you need to chain further queryset/model access rather than the cross-service JSON shape.

surface.name: nearby_rows_by_geohash
surface.intent: Same search as nearby_by_geohash but returns ORM Location rows (each carrying .distance_km) — for callers staying inside the ORM rather than consuming the JSON summary shape.

surface.name: radius
surface.intent: Every Location within radius_km of a point, ascending distance (membership, not top-K) — the in-process equivalent of the geo.radius comm Function. Call this instead of nearby() with a large limit and a manual distance filter, which is not the same query (nearby is top-K, this is membership).

surface.name: resolve
surface.intent: Resolve a Location UUID to a summary dict for cross-service reference checks (returns {found: false, ...} on a miss, never raises) — the in-process equivalent of the geo.resolve comm Function. Use this instead of a bare Location.objects.filter(uuid=...).first() when another module just needs to validate/expand a stored location_id.

requires.reason: comm bus (Functions geo.nearby/geo.radius/geo.bbox/geo.geohash_encode/geo.resolve), AppSettings config layer, flows, error registry (pyproject.toml dependency; conf.py:25, functions.py:25, flows.py:12, errors.py:6)
